subject: maths
question: Hema can do a certain piece of work in 30 days. Hema and Raji can together do the same work in 25 days, and Hema, Raji and Smitha can do the same work together in 10 days. In how many days can Hema and Smitha do the same work together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(30, 25, 10) = 150 units.

Efficiency: Hema = 5, Hema + Raji = 6, Hema + Raji + Smitha = 15.

Efficiency of Smitha = 15 − 6 = 9 units/day.

Time for Hema + Smitha = 150 ÷ (5 + 9) = 150/14 = 75/7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 75/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Hema = 30 days

Time taken by Hema + Raji = 25 days

Time taken by Hema + Raji + Smitha = 10 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Days**

 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Hema

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Smitha = Efficiency of (Hema + Raji + Smitha) − Efficiency of (Hema + Raji)

⇒ Efficiency of Smitha = 15 − 6 = 9 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of Hema + Smitha = 5 + 9 = 14 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Hema and Smitha together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 150 ÷ 14

⇒ Time = 75/7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 75/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Assumption

It is an effective practice to assume the Total Work to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given number of days to keep calculations simple and completely avoid dealing with fractions.

Pipes and Cisterns

The foundational concepts of Time & Work directly apply to Pipes and Cisterns, where an inlet filling a tank acts as positive work and an outlet emptying it acts as negative work.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed strictly in the ratio of the total work done. If multiple people work together for the exact same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.
